fair_value.method: Blend of forward P/E (50%), EV/sales (20%) and an FCF DCF (30%). The P/E leg is NTM EPS at Sep-2027 of about $10 (FY28 about $9.0 vs $9.63 consensus; FY29 about $11) x 23.5x = $235. EV/sales is $224 and the DCF is $205 after cutting FCF conversion and net cash, so the blend is about $224, down from $233 in round 1.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM non-GAAP EPS at Sep-2027 of about $10.0 (my FY28 $9.0 vs consensus $9.63; FY29 about $11.0) x 23.5x, cut from 24x. The discount to today's ~29x forward reflects decelerating growth, one direct customer at 43% of revenue and 57% of receivables, Marvell 1.6T AEC price competition, and peer multiple compression (Mizuho cut its target to $245 on lower peer multiples).

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: NTM revenue at Sep-2027 of about $4.3B (FY28 about $3.8-3.9B, +55%, consistent with consensus EPS; FY29 about $5B) x 10x = $43B, plus about $1.8B net cash (not $2B; cash plus investments is $764M post-DustPhotonics and Q1 OCF was only $90M), divided by about 200M diluted shares.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: FY28 FCF $1.25B (cut from $1.4B for the inventory build and working-capital drag; Q1 OCF $90M vs $236M non-GAAP NI, SBC about $88M/qtr). Growth 35/25/20/15/12/10/8% over years 2-8, then 4% terminal growth. WACC 11%. EV about $39.2B, plus $1.8B net cash, divided by 200M shares = about $205.

bear.story: The H2 FY27 ramp (H1 about $1.01B, so H2 needs about $1.47B, or ~23% q/q) slips, or the 43% direct customer (Amazon, Trn3) dual-sources 1.6T AECs to Marvell at 15-20% lower prices. FY28 EPS comes in around $7.5 and the multiple compresses to about 14-15x amid AI capex digestion talk.

base.story: FY27 revenue of about $2.5B (+85%) is delivered, and FY28 grows about 50-55% (about $3.8B) on optics, Active LED Cables and OmniConnect. Non-GAAP GM holds at 67-68%, but cash conversion lags on inventory. NTM EPS of about $10 at 23x.

bull.story: The 'outsized growth again' in FY28 beats the $9.63 consensus (EPS over $11). Amazon Trn3 ramps strongly in 2027 (Mizuho checks), and Microsoft, Meta and Oracle broaden the base. NTM EPS of about $13 at 27x, and the stock breaks the $308 high.

thesis_break_reason: $125 is about 17% below the verified $150.09 closing low of 2026-09-14 (intraday $149.14). That low came from a sentiment-only selloff after a beat-and-raise. $125 is also about 13x FY28 consensus EPS of $9.63. I moved down from $130 because, with ~90%+ realized vol, a level only ~13% under a recent capitulation low can be hit by noise alone. A close at $125 would most likely mean a top customer paused or dual-sourced (e.g. to Marvell 1.6T AECs), the H2 FY27 optical ramp failed, or a hyperscaler cut capex.

key_uncertainties: Whether H2 FY27 delivers about $1.47B of revenue (about 23% q/q growth) on the optical ramp
Customer concentration: end customers 33/28/13/10%; one direct customer is 43% of revenue and 57% of receivables
Marvell's 1.6T AEC/retimer lead and 15-20% lower pricing at Amazon; Amazon's warrants effectively rebate its AEC price
Cash conversion: Q1 OCF of $90M vs $236M non-GAAP NI, inventory at $313M, SBC about $88M per quarter
Pace of co-packaged optics adoption vs AEC/pluggable demand
Multiple regime: peer multiples are compressing, and the stock fell 52% then rebounded 41% in 9 sessions
reasoning: Round 1 facts stand: FY26 revenue $1.34B; Q1 FY27 $479M (+115%) at 68% non-GAAP GM; Q2 guided to $525-535M; FY27 >85% (about $2.5B; EPS consensus $6.31); FY28 consensus EPS about $9.63. The supervisor's checks endorsed my FY28 growth assumption (+50-60%, 'outsized growth again'), so I kept the EPS path. It also established three things that cut against my round-1 numbers, and I verified them. First, weak cash conversion: Q1 OCF was only $90.2M because inventory rose $62M to $313M. I therefore cut FY28 FCF to $1.25B and Sep-2027 net cash to about $1.8B, which lowers the DCF to $205 and EV/sales to $224. Second, heavier concentration: one direct customer is 43% of revenue. Third, credible Marvell competition on 1.6T AECs, with Mizuho cutting its target on lower peer multiples. Those justified trimming the P/E multiple to 23.5x ($235). The blended fair value falls from $233 to $224, about 6% above the $210.97 close. Scenarios are $110/$228/$350 at 27/48/25, a mean of about $226, with the bear weight raised for concentration and competition. For the ladder I used a lognormal with a median of about $214 (below fair value for execution risk) and a sigma of about 0.68, then trimmed the far right tail as in round 1 so the mean matches the scenarios. That gives P(>=211) of 0.51, P(<127) of 0.23 (slightly fatter than round 1's 0.21), and P(>=422) of 0.10. The analyst average target of about $280 (range $185-350) remains optimistic evidence. I used no options data; round 2 added 5 searches and fetches.
